routes.scope_locator: Preface through Basic Optical Laws, printed pp. 6-19
routes.reason: Gill assumes perspective knowledge and reiterates optical foundations; useful framing but not a new construction capability.

routes.scope_locator: Cone of Vision and One-Look, printed pp. 20-24
routes.reason: Adds a practical edge-distortion/single-view diagnostic, while the fixed numeric cone remains a theory hold.
This is Gill’s largest durable spatial delta: global near-to-far contrast/value/clarity grading tied to the same scene field.

routes.scope_locator: Shade and Shadow through The Drawing, printed pp. 52-81
routes.reason: The book supplies a coherent construction-to-render preparation workflow and reflected-light caveats; the exact tonal ranking is held rather than promoted.
Contrast hierarchy is useful for focus/depth but is better handled as a patch/context note than a new universal composition card.

routes.scope_locator: Cylinders, Cones and Spheres, printed pp. 91-117
routes.reason: Most form modeling generalizes the light/shade preparation and material-response patterns; shape-specific duplicates are unnecessary.

routes.scope_locator: Rendering Glass and Water, printed pp. 118-137
routes.reason: These chapters provide strong variants for a single broader material-response Pattern: transparency/reflection/background/view-angle/surface-state logic.

routes.scope_locator: Rocks through Floor Coverings, printed pp. 139-154
routes.reason: Texture examples reinforce informed observation and material cues but do not change the broader material decision.
Simple cube/cut-block repetition is worth a transient drill; the medium-specific dry-transfer material is reference only.

routes.scope_locator: Sciagraphy, Overlapping, Getting It All Together, printed pp. 170-180
routes.reason: Sciagraphy is a niche orthographic specialization and overlap already has a canonical Hogarth foundation; the final exercise mainly validates cue integration.

routes.scope_locator: Examples, Style, Final Statement, Glossary/back matter, printed pp. 181-214
routes.reason: Examples validate portability and communication goals but add no independent reusable Perspective/rendering mechanism.

rationale: Gill earns a Review + selective Deep PASS. Atmospheric effect and the pre-render light/shadow workflow are deep enough to survive as new capabilities; material behavior and the block drill are targeted; perspective basics, shape-specific examples, sciagraphy, overlap, and late style examples remain reference.
